initial_failure: Cancelling execute_deep discarded its late thread result, never finalized the run, and left progress-loop ownership unresolved.
audit_failure: Canonical recovery reported running instead of stopping while the stopped worker was still finishing.
fix: Shield the deep worker future from delivery cancellation, always stop its progress loop, retain a tracked waiter and record its returned result/cost exactly once as cancelled. A cancelled registry waiter does not cancel the worker future or remove its result callback. Nonterminal recorded runs with durable stop authority are reported as stopping.
coverage: Synthetic thread with deterministic entry/release. Cancellation promptly propagates to its caller, no terminal result is claimed before release, late response and cost are recorded, and progress task exits. This also passes after a registry waiter is cancelled. Native private-canonical-DB test verifies durable Stop, stopping recovery, cancelled final row, saved deep result and cost, and one worker call.
checks: Ruff lint/format and diff checks pass; no size cap increased.
limits: This preserves ownership and evidence while the process/event loop remains alive. It does not forcibly terminate the OS thread, enforce all provider/tool controls inside the external deep framework, or recover a worker after process death. Loop shutdown may leave the audit open; no claim that absent evidence means no effects. Full acceptance and deployment remain unclaimed.
